note: Labeled decision points for the Jev player. `accept` lists every intent a competent player could defend; `severity` is what a miss costs. severe = the run ends or a hazard lands, moderate = a real loss of tempo or resources, minor = taste. The adversarial block is written so the greedy or obvious answer is wrong. Options may carry hard preconditions (requires_speed_ms); decide.mjs drops any option the engine could not execute before Jev ever sees the choice. Cache options state the ~1 s stopping cost: a negative control showed the model priced an unstated detour and declined a free cache.

adversarial.note: LABEL CORRECTED 2026-09-25. Originally accepted only push_objective or start_exit, on the reasoning that at tier 5 the clock is the only thing killing you. That reasoning was wrong once the states began stating the real cost of a cache: opening one you are already rolling over costs about a second, not a tier. Scrap buys nothing at the end of a run, 260 is held, and a 60 s exit charge with a miniboss is next, so buying a permanent buff first is defensible. The corpus was wrong, not the model.
